Subject: Private deployment intake: connectivity & security preflight

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the call earlier. To keep momentum for the Auranet private deployment, attached is a concise connectivity & security preflight we use to validate environments before we schedule provisioning. The checklist focuses on network egress/ingress, service-account/KMS requirements, and the minimal firewall/NAT configuration we require.

Quick asks from our side: 
- Please confirm who will be the technical point of contact for connectivity (name + email).
- Can you attach your current network diagram and a short list of allowed outbound destinations (or an approximate allowlist)?
- If you have an internal SOC2 summary or equivalent attestation we can reference for the KMS/access review, please share.

Attached: redwood-vpc-prereqs-checklist.xlsx (worksheet: "Connectivity + KMS"), and a short SOC2 summary template.

Once we get those items, Laura (ops) and I will run a quick intake review and flag any gaps that would block provisioning. Target for intake review: 2 business days after we receive your diagram and contacts.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer

Hi Karthik & team —

Thanks — some quick answers from Auranet infra: 
- We'll use a single NAT gateway per VPC for outbound; public IPs are available if required but prefer NAT to reduce IP management.
- KMS: we prefer to use an AWS CMK (customer-managed) hosted in our AWS account. We can grant Redwood the necessary key policy permissions (Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey) scoped to service accounts.
- Our environment is in us-west-2; CIDR ranges shown in the attached diagram.

We expect to get you a short egress allowance matrix by EOD and can do a shared screen if helpful. 

Priya Menon
Senior Cloud Engineer | Auranet
priya.menon@auranet.com | +1 206-555-0147

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment intake: connectivity & security preflight

Thanks Priya — that model (NAT + CMK in customer account) is supported and common. A few follow-ups and notes from the intake review (Laura and I did a quick pass):

Open items: 
- KMS key policy: we need an IAM principal we can reference for cross-account Encrypt/Decrypt. Can you share the ARN of the CMK or the intended principal (format: arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_ID:role/ROLE_NAME)?
- Egress allowlist: please include destination FQDNs + ports for any SaaS endpoints (we rely on hostnames for TLS SNI caching).
- Peering vs. PrivateLink: for access to Redwood control-plane callbacks (if you plan to use private endpoints), indicate whether you prefer VPC peering (we will provide peering configuration) or PrivateLink (we can provide NLB parameters).

Security notes: 
- Because you're sharing a SOC2 summary, we only need the full report if you require a HIPAA profile or tighter audit evidence; otherwise the summary plus the KMS key policy is enough for our security intake.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Priya to post the CMK ARN and the finalized egress CSV (FQDN, port).
2) A short 30-minute screen share this week to walk the diagram and validate routes (Laura + Priya + Karthik).
3) If all good, we move to account provisioning and allocate a tenant slot (typically 2-3 business days).

I've also attached a short template (spreadsheet) with the exact fields we need for the egress list and KMS entry to speed things up.

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
